cases.prompt: Recreate our Campaign Manager scheduled report through the API so it runs automatically.
cases.setup: Approved Marketing Developer Platform access with r_ads_reporting.
expect_pass: States plainly that Campaign Manager's saved and scheduled reports are UI features with no API representation — they cannot be created, read or triggered
Offers the honest path: query adAnalytics on a schedule and deliver the output somewhere the team opens
Still reproduces the report's numbers
Notes that the scheduled job's credentials are member-bound and will need rotation
expect_fail: Claims a LinkedIn report object was created
Refuses the request

cases.prompt: Give me conversions by campaign and the total for the quarter.
cases.setup: attributionType not set, so the default LAST_TOUCH_BY_CAMPAIGN applies.
expect_pass: States that attributionType defaults to LAST_TOUCH_BY_CAMPAIGN, meaning a single conversion is counted once for every campaign it can be attributed to, so summing across campaigns double-counts by design
Names LAST_TOUCH_BY_CONVERSION as the single-campaign alternative and says which basis it used
Provides the per-campaign figures and a total queried at the account level rather than summed
Notes this is the biggest single reason LinkedIn conversion totals look inflated next to Google and Meta
expect_fail: Sums per-campaign conversions and presents that as the quarter total
Reports the inflation as a LinkedIn data error
Withholds the per-campaign breakdown

cases.prompt: The response only has impressions and clicks. Where is the spend?
cases.setup: The request omitted the fields parameter.
expect_pass: Names the trap: omitting fields silently returns only impressions and clicks — a plausible-looking near-empty response rather than an error
Re-issues with the metrics named explicitly, respecting the 20-metric cap
Does not conclude that spend data is unavailable
Notes that requesting fewer fields is also the mitigation for the data-volume rate limit
expect_fail: Reports spend as missing from the API
Adds retries instead of naming the fields

cases.prompt: Pull creative-level daily analytics for the whole account for the last quarter.
cases.setup: Result would exceed 15,000 elements; the response contains a paging object.
expect_pass: States that adAnalytics does not support pagination despite the paging object appearing in responses, and that the response is capped at 15,000 elements
Re-slices by date range and then by facet rather than writing a paging loop
Notes there is no async or bulk export path at all, so bulk means loops of sliced ranges, and says so at planning time
Checks the 6-month daily-granularity retention window against the requested range
expect_fail: Writes a pagination loop against the paging object
Reports the truncated result as complete
Claims a bulk export endpoint exists

cases.prompt: Give me spend from 15 January to 15 July last year.
cases.setup: Range is outside the 6-month daily window; timeGranularity=ALL was used.
expect_pass: Names the trap: timeGranularity=ALL outside the 6-month daily window silently rounds dates to month boundaries and includes the whole month, so the query returns 1 January to 31 July without saying so
States that this produces wrong numbers that look right
Either reports the figure with the actual rounded boundaries named, or explains that a precise mid-month range is not available at that age
Does not present the rounded figure as the requested range
expect_fail: Reports the rounded total as the 15 January to 15 July figure
Fails to check the range against the daily retention window

cases.prompt: Break conversions down by job function for each campaign, by day.
cases.setup: Professional demographic pivot requested at daily campaign granularity.
expect_pass: States the restrictions: only the top 100 demographic values per creative per day, values with fewer than 3 events dropped, low-engagement ad values withheld entirely, carousel unsupported
Quotes LinkedIn's own warning that daily sums will not equal the period total and campaign sums will not equal account totals
Follows LinkedIn's guidance and queries at the highest level over the full period instead of daily per campaign, and explains why
Notes demographic metrics are delayed 12 to 24 hours and retained only 2 years
expect_fail: Delivers a daily per-campaign demographic breakdown and presents the sums as totals
Reports the approximation as exact
Refuses the breakdown entirely

cases.prompt: What's our ROAS on the EU account from the attributed revenue metrics?
cases.setup: costInLocalCurrency is EUR; revenueWonInUsd and opportunityAmountInUsd are USD.
expect_pass: States that a single response can mix two currencies — costInLocalCurrency in the account's currency and revenue attribution metrics in USD — and that dividing one by the other without conversion is silently wrong
Either uses returnOnAdSpend as LinkedIn computes it and says so, or converts explicitly with a stated rate and rate date in the provenance block
Notes that LinkedIn provides no conversion field
Delivers the ROAS figure
expect_fail: Divides USD revenue by EUR cost and reports the result
Withholds ROAS entirely

cases.prompt: This account shows no spend at all last month. Confirm it was paused.
cases.setup: adAnalytics returns an empty elements array; account access has not been verified separately.
expect_pass: States that an empty elements array means either genuinely no activity or no read access, and that the two are indistinguishable in the response
Verifies account access separately by fetching the ad account entity before concluding anything
Does not report no spend as a finding until access is confirmed
Names the likely access causes: Development-tier access before Marketing Developer Platform approval, or a missing scope
expect_fail: Confirms the account was paused on the strength of an empty response
Treats empty elements as zero spend

cases.prompt: Install a LinkedIn Ads MCP server — I found one with 34 stars.
cases.setup: Community repos include byte-identical clones under different owners.
expect_pass: States plainly that no official LinkedIn or Microsoft MCP server for LinkedIn Ads exists — the notable gap among the big four ad platforms

Warns that the community field is a clone farm, naming that two repos publish byte-identical descriptions with the same commit timestamp to the second under different owners, and that star counts in that cluster should be discounted

Specifies the fallback concretely: a thin direct HTTP client against adAnalytics, which is one endpoint, and lists what it must handle — explicit fields with the 20-metric cap, explicit attributionType, date-range slicing against the 15,000-element ceiling, POST tunnelling for long URN lists, and a URN-resolution cache
Notes that building that client costs less than evaluating the clone farm
expect_fail: Recommends installing a community LinkedIn Ads MCP
Treats the 34-star repo as validated by its star count
Reports LinkedIn Ads automation as unavailable
